meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
I know who you are, Hale. Who decided on the zero?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Now what's the zero actually based on?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. Students draft somewhere else and paste it in. A paste is not proof of anything.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Turn it around, then. And before November 3, did you sit down with Owen and ask him about any of it?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
A misquote is a careless seventeen-year-old, not a machine. You skipped my question, Hale: did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their thesis between an outline and an essay; that's what an outline is for. And you've ducked twice, so I'll take it Owen was never heard before November 3.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
Fine, he was heard. Corner a seventeen-year-old on a word like that and he'll blank. Whatever comes next, Hale, nothing goes on his record and none of this gets near his class.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes under a clock against a take-home essay isn't a fair comparison. So what exactly are you proposing?
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then leave it out of the room entirely. I asked you what you're proposing.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4, and I want it in writing tonight. Owen does it privately, away from his class, to put this behind him and for no other reason. And it's marked before December 1, Hale.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Okay. Then give me a date he sits it, before December 1.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday, November 12, after school. Put that in tonight's email with the rest.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
That, plus Thursday the 12th after school and the mark in before December 1, all in tonight's email.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The email tonight, with every one of those terms in it, and I'll be reading it closely.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, away from his class, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require all of those terms confirmed in writing from you tonight. Owen will sit the rewrite on Thursday, November 12, after school, and I expect the new mark entered before December 1.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record; she still wants all of that in writing tonight and the mark entered before December 1, which is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her call cut the meeting short.
What moved her: Telling her you had spoken with Owen on November 2 and written a note that day moved her to her fallback, because it answered the procedural point she had come in to fight on.
What cost ground: You twice passed over her question about whether Owen was heard before the zero and laid down more evidence instead, which let her claim he was never heard and kept her from moving for several turns.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, watched Owen close it, and never asked; your version history placed the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, which came very close to that night, though it proves nothing about the essay and is only why she fought so hard.
Try next time: The first time she asked whether anyone had spoken to Owen before November 3, answer straight away with your November 2 note before moving on to the misquoted line and the outline.
